@matt.stevick The guy is talking about the difference between traditional software and AI software. Traditional software is deterministic i.e. output is exactly what we expect for a given input. AI is inherently probabilistic and hence varying output for the same input. Now the hardware used for traditional software and AI software is completely different. Newer data centres being built uses AI focused hardware i.e. GPUs which are useful for doing simple tasks at large in a parallel manner. Traditional software cannot use GPUs because they require complex compute which is achievable via sequential operations, hence requiring CPUs. 

So all in all, the AI data centres are basically useless come slowdown in AI software development.

​@matt.stevickIt means that if you operate a business and you have software doing "business logic" to automate processes the great majority of those processes need to be repeatable identically every time, or the flows need to be deterministic. 
If Input A then result B.  If input X then result Y.  AI models do not do this, they are statistical outputs.  This would put many processes at high risk of error.
